title: Time-Reversal-Invariant Altermagnetic Acoustic Crystals
authors: Tianzhi Xia, Han-Rong Xia, Jinglin Liu, Xiying Fan, Zebin Zhu, Zhen Gao
abstract: Altermagnets have emerged as a new class of magnetic materials that combine spin-split electronic bands with zero net magnetization. Extending this paradigm to classical-wave systems has, however, been fundamentally challenging because conventional realizations require broken time-reversal symmetry (TRS). Here, we overcome this limitation by introducing two pseudospin degrees of freedom and constructing a pseudo-time-reversal operator that faithfully reproduces the action of its physical counterpart while preserving actual TRS. Building on this framework, we theoretically propose and experimentally realize the first time-reversal-invariant altermagnetic acoustic crystal. Acoustic measurements directly reveal pseudospin-dependent band splitting--a defining hallmark of altermagnetism--under strictly TRS-preserving conditions. Moreover, the altermagnetic acoustic crystal exhibits sublattice-pseudospin locking, enabling flexible control over acoustic pseudospin splitting and filtering. Our work establishes acoustic crystals as a versatile platform for exploring altermagnetic physics and opens new avenues for spin-inspired wave manipulation in nonmagnetic devices.
summary: The paper introduces a novel acoustic crystal model that mimics the physics of altermagnets while strictly preserving Time-Reversal Symmetry. By using pseudospin degrees of freedom, they demonstrate measurable signatures like pseudospin splitting and directional filtering in sound waves. This establishes acoustic crystals as a versatile platform for exploring spin-inspired wave manipulation in nonmagnetic devices.
main_problem: The core challenge is extending altermagnetism—a state with spin-split bands but zero net magnetization—to classical wave systems while strictly preserving Time-Reversal Symmetry (TRS).
main_result: The authors successfully demonstrated the first time-reversal-invariant altermagnetic acoustic crystal, showing pseudospin splitting and orthogonal directional transport under TRS-preserving conditions.
method: Theoretical modeling uses a tight-binding Hamiltonian with pseudospin degrees of freedom, complemented by experimental characterization using 2D spatial Fourier transforms of measured sound-pressure fields.
model_or_system: The system is an acoustic crystal based on a bilayer-centered square lattice. The model incorporates pseudospin ($\uparrow/\downarrow$) and utilizes a pseudo-time-reversal operator to maintain true TRS while modeling altermagnetic physics.
key_observables: Pseudospin-dependent band splitting, anisotropic iso-frequency contours showing orthogonal elongation, and spatially separated acoustic field distributions corresponding to different pseudospins.

main_assumptions: The method relies on introducing a pseudospin degree of freedom and constructing a pseudo-time-reversal operator to circumvent the need for genuine TRS breaking in classical wave systems.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate band structures, constant-energy contours showing orthogonal splitting, and experimental measurements confirming sublattice-spin locking and the spatial separation of propagating acoustic fields along perpendicular axes ($x$ vs $y$).
paper_structure: The paper first introduces the theoretical framework using pseudospin to model altermagnetism in acoustics. It then details the experimental realization and measurement techniques, culminating in demonstrations of pseudospin splitting, sublattice-spin locking, and directional pseudospin filtering.
why_interesting: This work provides a concrete, non-electronic platform (acoustics) to study complex quantum magnetic phenomena like altermagnetism without breaking fundamental symmetries, offering insights applicable to phononics and mechanical wave engineering.
